title: Transcriptomic age from bulk RNA-seq with tAge
text: tAge_preprocessing() filters low-expressed genes, maps mouse Entrez gene space, RLE-normalises, log-transforms, scales (per sample), applies YuGene transform, aligns clock gene list, centres data. Prediction uses scaled_diff yugene_diff representations.
code: tAge_eset <- tAge_preprocessing(   eset,   species = "mouse",   gene_mapping_type = "Ensembl",   verbose = FALSE ) #> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes names(tAge_eset) #> [1] "RLE_normalized"  "log_transformed" "scaled"          "scaled_diff"     #> [5] "yugene"          "yugene_diff"

text: published clocks live Zenodo; list R (reads bundled registry): download_clocks() fetches chosen set returns path column:
code: head(list_clocks(type = "EN", outcome = "Mortality")) #>                                               filename type   outcome #> 1        EN_Mortality_Mouse_Multitissue_scaleddiff.pkl   EN Mortality #> 2        EN_Mortality_Mouse_Multitissue_yugenediff.pkl   EN Mortality #> 3 EN_Mortality_Multispecies_Multitissue_scaleddiff.pkl   EN Mortality #> 4 EN_Mortality_Multispecies_Multitissue_yugenediff.pkl   EN Mortality #> 5            EN_Mortality_Rodents_Liver_scaleddiff.pkl   EN Mortality #> 6            EN_Mortality_Rodents_Liver_yugenediff.pkl   EN Mortality #>        species       tissue scaling lifespan_scaled #> 1        Mouse Multi-Tissue  Scaled           FALSE #> 2        Mouse Multi-Tissue  YuGene           FALSE #> 3 Multispecies Multi-Tissue  Scaled           FALSE #> 4 Multispecies Multi-Tissue  YuGene           FALSE #> 5      Rodents        Liver  Scaled           FALSE #> 6      Rodents        Liver  YuGene           FALSE clocks <- list_clocks(type = "EN", outcome = "Mortality",                       species = "Multispecies", tissue = "Multi-Tissue") clocks <- download_clocks(clocks, dest_dir = "clocks")  model_paths <- list(   scaled_diff = clocks$path[clocks$scaling == "Scaled"],   yugene_diff = clocks$path[clocks$scaling == "YuGene"] )

title: Transcriptomic age from single-cell RNA-seq (pseudobulk) with tAge
text: clocks trained bulk RNA-seq. apply single-cell data, aggregate cells pseudobulk samples, run standard bulk pipeline. tAge aggregates coverage — pseudobulk sample pools enough cells reach target read depth — robust fixed cells-per-sample cut-. walkthrough uses Tabula Muris Senis (GSM4505404). Requires Seurat (SeuratDisk reticulate+anndata read .h5ad).

what: 1. Load single-cell data into a Seurat object
title: Transcriptomic age from single-cell RNA-seq (pseudobulk) with tAge
text: tAge also provides load_h5ad_to_seurat() convenience wrapper.
code: library(tAge) library(Seurat) library(reticulate)  Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = ".venv/bin/python")  # Read an .h5ad via anndata and build a Seurat object ad    <- import("anndata") adata <- ad$read_h5ad("GSM4505404_tabula-muris-senis-droplet-official-raw-obj.h5ad")  counts <- Matrix::t(adata$X) rownames(counts) <- adata$var_names$to_list() colnames(counts) <- adata$obs_names$to_list()  seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(   counts    = counts,   meta.data = as.data.frame(adata$obs),   project   = "TabulaMurisSenis" )

title: Transcriptomic age from single-cell RNA-seq (pseudobulk) with tAge
code: selected_tissues <- c("Tongue", "Kidney", "Liver", "Heart") seurat_subset <- subset(seurat_obj, subset = tissue %in% selected_tissues)

title: Transcriptomic age from single-cell RNA-seq (pseudobulk) with tAge
text: Aggregate within unique combination grouping columns, pooling cells pseudobulk sample reaches coverage_threshold reads.
code: eset <- aggregate_on_obs_columns(   seurat_obj       = seurat_subset,   obs_column_names = c("age", "mouse.id", "tissue"),   coverage_threshold = 1e7,   verbose = TRUE )  # Simpler variant: aggregate the whole object by coverage only # eset <- aggregate_pseudobulk(seurat_subset, coverage_threshold = 1e6)

title: Transcriptomic age from single-cell RNA-seq (pseudobulk) with tAge
code: eset_clean <- remove_outliers(eset, split_by = "tissue") plot_eset_density(eset_clean)

title: Transcriptomic age from single-cell RNA-seq (pseudobulk) with tAge
text: tAge_by_group() runs preprocessing prediction separately within level split_by (recommended multi-tissue data).
code: # Download clocks (see the bulk vignette / ?download_clocks) clocks <- download_clocks(   list_clocks(type = "EN", outcome = "Chronological",               species = "Multispecies", tissue = "Multi-Tissue"),   dest_dir = "clocks" ) model_paths <- list(   scaled_diff = clocks$path[clocks$scaling == "Scaled"],   yugene_diff = clocks$path[clocks$scaling == "YuGene"] )  results <- tAge_by_group(   eset        = eset_clean,   split_by    = "tissue",   model_paths = model_paths,   species     = "mouse",   mode        = "EN" )

title: Transcriptomic age from single-cell RNA-seq (pseudobulk) with tAge
text: See bulk vignette (vignette("tage-bulk")) interpret output role reference groups (centring).
code: results$age_numeric <- as.numeric(gsub("m", "", results$age))  tage_boxplot(   results,   x_var        = "age",   y_var        = "scaled_diff_EN_tAge",   subgroup_var = "tissue",   stat_method  = "wilcox.test",   theme_type   = "bw",   title        = "Predicted tAge by age and tissue",   xlab         = "Chronological age",   ylab         = "Predicted tAge (months)" )

what: tAge — transcriptomic biological age in R
title: tAge — transcriptomic biological age in R
text: R package transcriptomic biological age prediction gene expression data, implementing transcriptomic clocks Tyshkovskiy et al. (2026), Nature. clocks predict two kinds biological age bulk RNA-seq (pseudobulk single-cell) expression: chronological age expected mortality. tAge handles preprocessing, normalisation, gene mapping across species, prediction pre-trained Elastic Net (EN) Bayesian Ridge (BR) models.

code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("Gladyshev-Lab/tAge")

title: tAge — transcriptomic biological age in R
text: tAge calls Python (via reticulate) run model predictions. Create virtual environment packages listed inst/python/requirements.txt: Point R interpreter calling predict_tAge():
code: python -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -r inst/python/requirements.txt   # joblib pandas scikit-learn numpy # Linux / macOS Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = ".venv/bin/python") # Windows Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = ".venv/Scripts/python.exe")

title: tAge — transcriptomic biological age in R
text: Models published Zenodo (record 18763485). can list download directly R:
code: library(tAge)  # Browse available clocks (filter by type / outcome / species / tissue / scaling) list_clocks(type = "EN", outcome = "Mortality")  # Download a chosen set; returns the table with a `path` column clocks <- list_clocks(type = "EN", outcome = "Mortality",                       species = "Multispecies", tissue = "Multi-Tissue") clocks <- download_clocks(clocks, dest_dir = "clocks")  model_paths <- list(   scaled_diff = clocks$path[clocks$scaling == "Scaled"],   yugene_diff = clocks$path[clocks$scaling == "YuGene"] )

title: tAge — transcriptomic biological age in R
code: library(tAge) Sys.setenv(RETICULATE_PYTHON = ".venv/bin/python")  # 1. Load raw counts (genes x samples) and sample metadata (samples x variables) exprs_data <- read.csv("expression_matrix.csv", row.names = 1) metadata   <- read.csv("metadata.csv", row.names = 1) eset <- make_ExpressionSet(exprs_data, metadata)  # 2. Preprocess: filter, map genes, RLE-normalise, log, scale, YuGene, centre tAge_eset <- tAge_preprocessing(   eset,   species = "mouse",   gene_mapping_type = "Gene.Symbol"    # or "Ensembl" )  # 3. Predict results <- predict_tAge(tAge_eset, model_paths, species = "mouse", mode = "EN") head(results)

title: tAge 1.1.0
text: Corrects three bugs produced wrong predictions 1.0.0 / 1.0.1. Analyses run versions repeated 1.1.0.

title: tAge 1.1.0
text: Species rescaling now applied chronological-age clocks. Previously every prediction multiplied species maximum-lifespan factor, turned mortality output (log10 hazard ratio) normalized-age output meaningless numbers. clock type taken model file name, matching TACO reference application. Reference centring never skipped. control_subtraction() used return data unchanged reference group given. distributed clocks relative (_scaleddiff / _yugenediff) models trained reference-centred expression, predictions made without centring invalid. column_name control_label now default NULL, centres samples (overall per-gene median) — TACO default. Genes absent input padded NA instead 0 aligning clock gene list. trained model’s imputer fills training-set median gene, correct neutral value. predict_tAge() coerces reticulate result data.frame, fixing failure reticulate/pandas versions return bare vector single-column result. tage_boxplot() exported.

title: tAge 1.1.0
text: Clock registry: list_clocks() browses pre-trained models (filter type, outcome, species, tissue scaling) download_clocks() fetches Zenodo record 18763485, returning table path column. registry ships package inst/extdata/clocks_metadata.csv.

title: tAge 1.1.0
text: Two vignettes replace former Jupyter notebooks: vignette("tage-bulk") bulk RNA-seq vignette("tage-singlecell") pseudobulk single-cell workflow. pkgdown site https://gladyshev-lab.github.io/tAge/. README rewritten: units clock outcome, role reference groups relative clocks, supported species, licensing. scale_eset() documents scaling per sample (column-wise, sample scaled across genes). Per-gene standardisation happens separately inside trained model, using training-set statistics.

title: tAge 1.1.0
text: testthat suite covering clock registry, prediction preprocessing.
